goal: Pilot first-time readers' actual ability to navigate L0 overview into historically meaningful L1 chapter and make a conceptual distinction, without claiming a psychometric survey.
suggestedPilotProcedure: Provide standalone HTML to a consenting adult reader and clarify it is a research draft, not a reviewed educational product.
Ask them to select ONE assigned volume, read L0 and navigate to the specified L1 chapter.
Observe whether they can locate the chapter and explain the historical distinction in their own words; do not coach answers.
Ask the two existing volume-specific comprehension questions and record unknown terminology and confusing transitions.
Have participant explicitly choose whether to export deidentified notes; do not upload individual responses to public GitHub.
Keep optional timing notes separately, distinguish navigation failure from historical misunderstanding, and record only real human responses.
Only after reviewing actual feedback and expert historical evidence, decide whether the specific L1 sentence should be rewritten.
